newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - GOLD SEEN CAPPED BY $330, PLATINUM LOWER.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - GOLD SEEN CAPPED BY $330, PLATINUM LOWER.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold price movements will depend on near term action in stock and currency markets, but resistance at $330 may be too stiff to hurdle, dealers said.
Platinum is down after an overnight settlement of the Impala strike but the downside is seen limited by tight supply.

GOLD - Prices have run into stubborn upside resistance and a better overnight session of the U.S. stock market after Friday's decline decreased the likelihood that bullion would build on last week's gains, dealers and analysts said.
"The Dow would have to go down another 100 points for gold to break above $330," a dealer said. "There's strong resistance at $328-$330 at the moment and personally I see it heading lower."
On the downside $323 would provide support, which if broken would target the recent low of $317, he said.
At 0745 GMT spot gold was quoted at $327.25/$327.75, down $0.95 from Monday's New York close.
PLATINUM - Sentiment was bruised but not too badly by late Monday's settlement between South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd and some 400 striking workers, dealers said.
Full production would resume on Tuesday morning after the strike was initiated on August 4, the company said.
"Platinum is down from last night and could lose another $10, maybe. Demand is very good and supply is very tight so the effect is not going to be huge," a dealer said.
"I don't see platinum much below $400 at all through the end of this year," he added.
Spot platinum was indicated at $436.00/$439.00 an ounce, compared to $442.00/$445.00 at Monday's New York close.
SILVER - Prices are tightly rangebound as the market has taken a more conservative stance than gold. On the upside $4.50 is proving difficult to surpass, dealers said.
Support is expected between $4.30 and $4.20.
Spot silver was last indicated at $4.43/$4.45, off two cents from Monday's New York close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
